articles.title: Biallelic RPE65 variants causing Leber congenital amaurosis: genotype-phenotype correlations and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Biallelic pathogenic variants in RPE65 cause Leber congenital amaurosis type 2 (LCA2) and early-onset severe retinal dystrophy (EOSRD). We describe the genotype-phenotype spectrum of 54 individuals with biallelic RPE65 variants from 43 unrelated families. The c.260A>G (p.Asp87Gly) missense variant was the most prevalent allele, present in 23% of families. Electroretinography was non-detectable in 89% of patients by age 10 years. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated preserved ellipsoid zone in 67% of patients under 12 years, with progressive attrition thereafter. All patients with preserved central photoreceptor structure and sufficient viable retinal cells were considered candidates for voretigene neparvovec gene therapy.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes of voretigene neparvovec gene therapy for RPE65-associated inherited retinal dystrophy.
articles.abstract: We report 5-year follow-up data from the phase 3 trial of voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna) in patients with biallelic RPE65-associated retinal dystrophy. Bilateral subretinal injection of AAV2-RPE65 was performed in 29 participants. The primary endpoint was multi-luminance mobility testing (MLMT). At year 5, MLMT score improved by a mean of 1.8 lux levels from baseline (p<0.001). Full-field stimulus testing (FST) thresholds were significantly improved in 93% of treated eyes. No serious adverse events attributable to the vector were observed. These data confirm durable efficacy and a favorable safety profile at 5 years post-treatment.

articles.title: Functional classification of RPE65 missense variants using a retinal pigment epithelium cell model.
articles.abstract: Missense variants in RPE65 present a classification challenge due to variable functional impact. We developed an RPE cell-based assay to quantify 11-cis-retinal production as a functional readout for 48 RPE65 missense variants of uncertain significance. The c.260A>G (p.Asp87Gly) variant retained 12% of wild-type enzymatic activity, consistent with a severely hypomorphic allele. Variants retaining less than 20% activity correlated with early-onset severe phenotypes (LCA2), while those retaining 20-60% activity were associated with later-onset rod-cone dystrophy. This cell model provides a reproducible functional framework to reclassify RPE65 VUS and predict disease severity.
